title: Break down a supply delivery at the clean-storage line
instruction: Unpack the brown carton on the left: put the brown cardboard insert on the dark grey pad, and pass the blue, green and orange boxes through the grey pass-through in the yellow partition onto the teal shelf on the right. When you finish, no brown cardboard may be over the pass-through or past the partition.
context: Hospital infection-control practice (AORN, AAMI ST79) requires corrugated shipping cartons and packing to be removed in a breakdown area before supplies enter clean or sterile storage, because cardboard carries dust, moisture and insects; staff unpack at the line and pass only the product boxes across. Done by: central sterile supply technicians, hospital materials handlers, stock clerks.
setup: A yellow partition (painted wood, 20 cm tall, 2 cm thick) stands on the table midline, halfway between the arm bases, running from 10 to 55 cm in front of them, with a 15 cm gap from 17.5 to 32.5 cm in front of them. In the gap sits a grey plastic pass-through shelf, 15 x 15 cm and 2 cm tall, centred on the midline 25 cm in front of the bases. On the robot's left, an opened brown corrugated shipping carton (outside 22.5 cm front to back, 15 cm side to side, walls 5 cm tall and 1 cm thick, 5 mm floor) is centred 30 cm straight in front of the left arm base. In it stand three cardboard supply boxes, 5.5 cm cubes of 80 g each, each one colour all over, in a row front to back 6.5 cm apart (centre to centre): blue nearest the arms (23.5 cm in front of the bases), green in the middle (30 cm), orange farthest (36.5 cm), each centred side to side in the carton. A brown corrugated cardboard insert (a folded block, 18 cm front to back, 6 cm side to side, 3 cm tall, 60 g) lies flat across the three boxes' tops, centred on the carton, long side front to back. A flat dark grey rubber breakdown pad (24 cm front to back, 10 cm side to side, 2 mm thick) lies between the carton and the partition, centred 32 cm in front of the bases and 14.5 cm left of the midline (16 cm right of the left arm base), so its right edge is 2 cm clear of the pass-through's left edge and its left edge 3.5 cm clear of the carton. On the robot's right, a teal plastic clean-supply shelf (a solid block, 22 cm front to back, 12 cm side to side, 6 cm tall) is centred 30 cm straight in front of the right arm base. The partition, pass-through, carton, pad and shelf are fixed to the table; the boxes and the insert are loose. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: An object is at rest when it moves under 1 cm/s and turns under 0.5 rad/s. A supply box counts as on the shelf when its whole footprint (its real outline from above, corners included however the box is turned, not a bounding box) is inside the shelf top's edges, its bottom is within 3 mm of the shelf top (standing on the shelf, not stacked, and not held in the air, even still and just above it), it lies on one of its faces (any face, since the boxes are one colour all over) tilted at most 10 degrees, and it is at rest: 0.3 each. The insert counts as on the pad when its centre is inside the pad's outline, its bottom is within 3 mm of the pad's top, its 18 x 6 cm face is down (either side) tilted at most 15 degrees, and it is at rest: 0.1. The cardboard rule is judged on the final state only (when the trial ends, at success or at the time limit), not on the path taken: if at the end of the trial any part of the insert is past the partition's left face (the plane 1 cm left of the midline), or any part of its real outline from above overlaps the pass-through's outline, at any height, the score is 0. Success, which ends the trial at 1.0: all three boxes on the shelf and the insert on the pad, as above, for 2.5 s. At the time limit the score is the sum of the credits above.
reset_notes: Stand the blue, green and orange boxes back in the carton at their marks (blue nearest the arms) and lay the insert flat across their tops, long side front to back. Tape marks on the carton floor make this quick; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate: the carton is fixed in place (tape it to the table for real trials) and the insert is one rigid block, so the carton can't be lifted and nothing folds. Dust and contamination aren't modelled; cardboard at or past the line stands in for them. The partition only has to stop the arms reaching over (20 cm). Every object, loose or fixed, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than cardboard or plastic.
